Randall Carlson returns to Danny Jones's podcast to present what he calls proof of ancient lightning bolt technology. In his reading, the evidence shows that earth's distant past held electrical forces and engineering. The standard timeline, he says, cannot explain them. The episode continues his long argument that ancient history is a record of catastrophe and lost knowledge.

Carlson builds from geology outward, as he prefers, pointing to landscapes and structures he believes only extreme energy can explain. Jones draws out the strongest examples. Mainstream science disputes both the readings and the conclusions, and Carlson's claims remain his own synthesis. What the recording offers is the master's class itself. The leading voice of catastrophist history lays out new material for his audience. He does it in the conversational form where his following actually meets him.

Astrophysicist Avi Loeb joins Joe Rogan to argue that the science world is not open minded in a segment from the show. Loeb is the Harvard scholar who hunts alien tech and roasts his peers for fear of the hunt. He brings that charge here.

Loeb tells how doors shut when he raised the alien case for a strange space rock. He argues grants and posts now punish bold claims. Rogan asks what a brave field would do instead. Listeners get Loeb's case in a tight, hot cut. The library holds the segment as an archive record of his stated views.

Joe Rogan turns to a claim that Bill Gates gave 319 million dollars to media outlets in a segment from his show. The point at issue is sway: what such gifts buy in the press. Rogan hosts the look at the claim.

Rogan works through the grants as they were found and asks what they mean for trust in news. He weighs how a rich man's gifts can bend what gets told and what gets left cold. The segment is short and sharp. Listeners get a brisk take on cash and press. The library holds the file as an archive record of the claim as stated.
podcast-joerogan-q8HRqmkEKWw:
Rock drummer Tommy Lee joins Joe Rogan for episode 2520. Lee co-founded Motley Crue and lived its wildest years in full. His name alone promises backstage chaos.

He shares tales of tours, excess, and survival in a hard business. Rogan, a longtime fan, draws out the stories behind the myth. They talk about fame gained young and the price it charged. The episode is pure rock nostalgia with a candid edge. Fans of the band get their drummer unplugged, older, and still entirely himself. Age has not tamed his tales or his grin.
